name: Medications
label: Dischord
lede: Two friends who'd been swapping instruments since high school, a band after Faraquet that took the math out of math rock, and a five-year gap that ended in the most tuneful record they ever made.

eras.title: Before the pills
eras.text: Dischord's bio says Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter had been swapping instruments and bands since high school in Los Angeles. In DC that partnership became Faraquet, a trio of knotted, shifting songs that set up everything Medications would do.

years.h: Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter form [[Faraquet|e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd]]
years.p: Devin Ocampo, then drumming in [[Smart Went Crazy|d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2]] in DC, meets bassist Jeff Boswell there; with Chad Molter they form Faraquet. Ocampo plays guitar, Molter drums.

years.h: Faraquet's The View from This Tower · Dischord
years.p: Faraquet's only album. A year later the band is done.

eras.title: A trio on Dischord
eras.text: With Chad Molter moved to bass and Andrew Becker on drums, Devin Ocampo and Molter started over. Medications toured the US and Europe hard and made two records in two years, the second produced by Fugazi's Brendan Canty.

years.h: Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter start Medications
years.p: [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] on guitar and vocals, [[Chad Molter|794c2243-0136-4627-887c-00749b81475d]] on bass and vocals, [[Andrew Becker|2eb6962f-0d20-4d8c-896b-c5ac3613377e]] on drums. The two Faraquet founders swap instruments again; the partnership doesn't change.
Medications' debut EP: five songs, exactly as the title says.

years.h: Your Favorite People All In One Place · Dischord 149
years.p: Medications' first full-length, recorded at Inner Ear and produced by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]].
years.xp: Ten songs, from Surprise! to Occupied, with Twine Time and This Is The Part We Laugh About in between.
play: Your Favorite People All In One Place

years.p: Devin Ocampo starts playing with Chad Clark, his old Smart Went Crazy bandmate, replacing Beauty Pill drummer Ryan Nelson. He's still in Beauty Pill two decades later.

eras.title: A course correction
eras.text: Drummer Andrew Becker left, Medications went quiet, and Faraquet briefly came back. When Medications returned in 2010 with multi-instrumentalist Mark Cisneros, the prog tangles were gone and the harmonies had moved to the front.

years.p: Faraquet, Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter's earlier band, reunite for shows in Brazil and DC. Dischord puts out Faraquet's Anthology 1997–98 in 2008.
Mark Cisneros joins on keys, clarinet and whatever else the songs need. Washington City Paper reported that Chad Molter covered the drums in the studio after Becker's exit.

years.h: Completely Removed, Medications' second album · Dischord No. 165
years.p: Out five years after Your Favorite People All In One Place. Devin Ocampo recorded it himself over several months, instead of the band's usual live-in-the-studio approach, and stacked the vocals high.
years.xp:
Washington City Paper called it a course correction of the most tuneful variety, and one of the finest records out of the city's punk community in ages.

The self-recording gave Ocampo room for layered harmonies and multi-tracked vocal arrangements that the earlier, knottier records never had.

years.p: Dischord lists Medications as active 2003–2011. There's no farewell show on record; the band just stops.

eras.title: Back to Faraquet
eras.text: Neither man stopped. Ocampo kept playing with Beauty Pill and started The Effects; Molter went solo as Whisper States. Then the band before Medications came back.

years.p: Devin Ocampo, Chad Molter and Jeff Boswell announce summer and fall Faraquet dates, their first run since 2008.
